Ibn Baz: a Muslim on a plane or in the desert must try to learn the qibla by asking those who know or by looking at its signs. If that is not possible, he makes ijtihad and prays, and his prayer is valid even if it later proves mistaken. If there is enough time, there is no harm in delaying until landing. In voluntary prayers — on a plane, in a car or on a mount — facing the qibla is not required; if easy, it is recommended to face it at the opening takbir.

Ibn Baz: he prays according to his ability — standing with bowing and prostration if he can, as on a ship; if not, seated, by gestures. He faces the qibla and turns with the plane as it changes course. For voluntary prayers, facing the direction of flight is enough.

Ibn Baz: prayers with a cause (tahiyyat al-masjid, the prayer after tawaf, the eclipse prayer) may be prayed even at the forbidden times. For one who enters after Asr or Fajr, the better course is to pray two rak‘ahs and not sit before them.
Ibn Baz: praying an obligatory prayer without trying to determine the direction is not allowed, and (if the direction turns out wrong) it must be repeated.

Ibrahim, together with his son Ismail, raised the foundations of the House (the Kaaba). While working they made dua: “Our Lord, accept this from us! You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Make us Muslims, submitting to You.”

Ibrahim’s people worshipped idols made of stone. He broke the idols, leaving only the biggest one. The Prophet ﷺ came to Abu Bakr’s house in the midday heat, at an unusual hour, and told him permission to emigrate had been given. Abu Bakr asked to be his companion; two camels had been prepared in advance.
The Prophet ﷺ did not fast in any month, other than Ramadan, as much as he fasted in Sha‘ban (al-Bukhari 1969).
The Prophet ﷺ gently told the boy in his care: “Young boy, mention Allah’s name, eat with your right hand and eat from what is in front of you” (al-Bukhari 5376).
The Prophet ﷺ kissed his grandson al-Hasan; to a man who said he had never kissed any of his ten children he said: “Whoever shows no mercy will be shown no mercy” (al-Bukhari 5997).

The Prophet ﷺ loved to begin with the right in all his affairs (al-Bukhari 426). On this basis scholars consider it recommended to enter the mosque with the right foot and leave with the left. On entering and leaving one says the duas the Prophet ﷺ taught:
The Prophet ﷺ mentioned a man on a long journey, dishevelled, raising his hands to the sky: “O Lord, O Lord” — while his food, drink and clothing are unlawful: how can he be answered? (Muslim 1015).

The Prophet ﷺ ordered the Companions who had not brought sacrificial animals to turn their ihram into Umrah (al-Bukhari 1568). For this reason Ibn Baz and Ibn Uthaymin consider tamattu‘ the best for one who has not brought an animal.
The Prophet ﷺ said he was about to burn the houses of men who stayed away from the congregation (Bukhari 644), and that the heaviest prayers for the hypocrites are Fajr and Isha (Bukhari 657).

• Some researchers and the Islamic Organization for Medical Sciences considered it pure — so the matter is disputed.
